name: LaserPecker 4
tagline: Ultra-portable laser for on-the-go engraving and small gifts
tldr: A compact, foldable diode laser designed for portability : markets, events, and desk gifts. Dual laser sources in the Pro model. Not a workshop production machine, but unmatched for throwing in a bag and engraving on-site.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

pros: 2W on LaserPecker 4: engraving-first : photo fills and leather at moderate speeds
Open-frame : plan laser glasses, exhaust, and workspace rules from day one

LaserPecker 4 : full profile with material limits and benchmarks on Maker Atlas
cons: Targets thin cuts (about 4 mm basswood class) : not thick production plywood
Not the SKU for a shop cutting 4 mm+ stock all day

beginnerNotes: This profile covers LaserPecker 4. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks before buying, then compare nearby models on the Compare page.
proTips: Use the slide extension for longer items. Battery pack (if available for your model) is essential for markets. Pre-test designs on sample materials : on-site failures are embarrassing.
primaryUse: Portable on-site engraving of small items at events, gifts, and personal travel projects.

faq.question: Can LaserPecker 4 be my first laser?
faq.answer: Only if portability is your primary need. For learning laser craft at home, a larger bench machine like Ortur LM3 or xTool D1 Pro offers far more capability for similar or lower cost.

faq.question: Does it work on metal?
faq.answer: The Pro model can mark some metals with limitations. It is not a fiber laser : expect lighter marks than dedicated metal machines like xTool F1 Ultra.

mainObjective: Portable on-site engraving for events and small items

editorialDepth.advantages: LaserPecker 4 2W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 4 mm+ cutting in production. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.
